resourceProfile.assessment: The complete English and Vietnamese source scope, review metadata, glossary, and project concept references were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review metadata, queue validation, typecheck, 79 test files with 462 tests, complete build, 39 IIS rules with 61 route cases, and 724 generated-link checks passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A bounded Vietnamese pass identified 25 actionable technical translation defects; all 25 were corrected.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Vietnamese human review was performed in this cycle; changed IDs remain machine-drafted.

publicationAuthorization.summary: No merge, publication, deployment, or residual-risk authorization was requested or granted.

findings.summary: The Ohm formula translated the current variable as a Vietnamese pronoun.
evidence: The formula must retain the symbol I.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard variable I.

findings.summary: The current definition repeated the Vietnamese word for ampere.
evidence: The source defines I as current measured in amperes.
findings.resolution: Used natural Vietnamese wording with the A unit.

findings.summary: Both rearranged Ohm formulas localized I as text, making the equations invalid.
evidence: The formulas solve for current and resistance.
findings.resolution: Restored I and standardized division spacing.

findings.summary: The resistance example title was a literal and awkward phrase.
evidence: The example finds resistance.
findings.resolution: Changed the title to the natural Vietnamese term for finding resistance.

findings.summary: The section title said electrical energy while the section defines electrical power.
evidence: The section uses P = V × I and reports watts.
findings.resolution: Changed the title to electrical power.

findings.summary: The concept name translated heating as domestic warming.
evidence: The concept is Joule heating in an electrical resistance.
findings.resolution: Changed the display name to the Vietnamese technical term for Joule heating.

findings.summary: The heading and first formula contained awkward heating wording and a localized current variable.
evidence: The section defines electrical heating power.
findings.resolution: Corrected the heading and restored I in the formula.

findings.summary: The I bullet had incorrect Vietnamese grammar.
evidence: The bullet defines current in amperes.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a complete technical definition.

findings.summary: The conclusion expressed power as joules per second without clearly separating energy and power.
evidence: The calculation gives 7.2 W and 72 J over 10 seconds.
findings.resolution: Separated the power result from the total energy result.

findings.summary: The branch definition used an unnatural current-path phrase.
evidence: A branch is a path between two circuit nodes.
findings.resolution: Rewrote it as a current path between two nodes.

findings.summary: The title translated current law as a law about what is current.
evidence: The section is Kirchhoff's current law.
findings.resolution: Changed the title to the standard Vietnamese circuit term.

findings.summary: The KCL formula localized I as a word and was no longer a valid equation.
evidence: KCL requires the current symbol I.
findings.resolution: Restored Σ I = 0.

findings.summary: Series and parallel equations localized I_total and R_total as prose.
evidence: The equations must retain the variable names used by the calculator concepts.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard total-current and total-resistance variables.

findings.summary: The formula mixed Vietnamese prose into a symbolic parenthetical label.
evidence: The source uses a stable parenthetical description for parallel branches.
findings.resolution: Restored the concise symbolic label.

findings.summary: The series and parallel labels in the cell equations were inconsistent with the formula vocabulary.
evidence: The source distinguishes series voltage addition from parallel capacity addition.
findings.resolution: Restored the standard series and parallel labels.

findings.summary: All three trigonometry formulas used localized side names that made the technical equations fragile and ambiguous.
evidence: SOH-CAH-TOA requires the exact opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse roles.
findings.resolution: Restored the canonical side names in all three equations.

findings.summary: The inverse-trigonometry formulas used localized side names rather than stable technical variables.
evidence: Inverse sine, cosine, and tangent must use the corresponding side ratios.
findings.resolution: Restored the canonical side names in all three inverse formulas.

findings.summary: Doubling mass was said to double thermal power instead of heat capacity.
evidence: The section distinguishes object heat capacity from material specific heat capacity.
findings.resolution: Corrected the conclusion to heat capacity.

findings.summary: L was translated as specific heat capacity rather than specific latent heat.
evidence: The formula Q = m × L describes phase-change energy.
findings.resolution: Translated L as specific latent heat.

findings.summary: The Vietnamese text did not consistently distinguish heat-flux density from total heat transfer.
evidence: q'' is measured in W/m² and A is an area.
findings.resolution: Used heat-flux density terminology and corrected square-metre units.

findings.summary: The worked heat-flux example omitted superscript formatting in the area units.
evidence: The example divides 100 W by 0.020 m².
findings.resolution: Restored m² and W/m² formatting.

findings.summary: The conduction heading was translated as electrical conduction and the formula mixed localized and English temperature names.
evidence: The section concerns heat conduction through a plane layer.
findings.resolution: Changed the heading to heat conduction and restored stable formula variables.

findings.summary: The practical check referred to thermal energy where heat capacity is needed to calculate temperature change.
evidence: Heat flux is a transfer rate, while heat capacity relates energy to temperature change.
findings.resolution: Rewrote the instruction to use heat capacity.

findings.summary: The SI base-unit table contained mistranslated symbols and names for metre, second, amount of substance, and candela.
evidence: The SI symbols must be m, s, mol, and cd.
findings.resolution: Corrected the affected Vietnamese names and symbols.

findings.summary: The amount-of-substance row used the Vietnamese word for a mole animal rather than the SI unit mol.
evidence: The SI base quantity is amount of substance and its unit is the mole, symbol mol.
findings.resolution: Changed the row to the technical unit name and symbol.
